name: Iphdeiah
overview: Iphdeiah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, known specifically as the son of Shashak. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional personal details or notable deeds recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Iphdeiah means 'YHWH redeems,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names that acknowledge God's saving work. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:25.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Iphdeiah explicitly as the son of Shashak. Beyond this direct paternal relationship, no other family connections or relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Iphdeiah's significance lies chiefly in his place within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, as preserved in 1 Chronicles. His mention helps maintain the continuity of the tribe's lineage, which is important for understanding the fulfillment of God's promises to Israel. Though no further narrative details are given, his inclusion underscores the biblical emphasis on heritage and divine redemption.
